title: customer escalation war-room: acme payments - prep & action items
content:
Purpose / quick summary:
- Prep notes for war-room with Acme Payments (customer-facing P1).
- Goal: align cross-functional responders, confirm rollback/fallback plan, prepare customer comms, capture actions + owners.
- Meeting scheduled: 2026-03-04 09:30 PT (30m) -> follow-up 10:15 PT if needed.

Problem statement (short):
- Since ~2026-03-03 22:10 PT, Acme reports elevated inference latency and 15% request error rate for their payment-authorization route using model 'redwood-rt-1.3'. Errors are 500s from inference runtime and occasional timeouts upstream.
- Customer impact: aborted payment flows, several customers reporting failed transactions (CS reported ~120 failed attempts in last 2 hrs).

Known facts / data points to surface in war-room:
- Last successful deploy of redwood-rt-1.3 -> 2026-03-01 02:00 PT. No config changes since.
- CPU/GPU utilization: spikes on dedicated pool 'dedicated-acme-1' (see Grafana dashboard ACME-DEDI-POOL).
- Error pattern: backend returns "kv cache miss" followed by 500 in ~40% of failed requests. (Need to verify with serving-runtime logs).
- Affected routes: /v1/generate (customer route: acme-auth-v1).
- SLOs breached: 99p latency target 300ms -> currently 95p ~720ms; error rate > 5% threshold.

Telemetry & queries to run at start (have these ready):
- k8s pods: kubectl -n dedicated-acme get pods -o wide | grep redwood-runtime
- tail runtime logs (last 60m): kubectl -n dedicated-acme logs -l app=redwood-runtime --since=60m | egrep "ERROR|kv cache|timeout|OOM"
- query tracing: tracing service (jaeger): service=redwood-runtime spanName=generate filter=error
- grafana: ACME-DEDI-POOL -> cpu/gpu utilization, queue length, per-route p50/p95/p99
- redis/kv cache hits: redis-cli -h kv-cache-acme INFO; keyspace hits/misses
- metrics: prometheus query for 5m error rate: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="runtime",route="acme-auth-v1",code!~"2.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="runtime",route="acme-auth-v1"}[5m]))

Initial triage hypotheses (to test in first 10 min):
1) KV cache corruption or eviction behaviour after recent model warm-up -> causing cache misses and regen overhead.
2) Autoscaler misconfiguration -> too aggressive downscale leaving warmup latency on spike.
3) Model variant regression (weights change or quantization bug) introduced in latest model build.
4) Underlying infra (GPU driver/kernel) causing intermittent failures -> check nodal OOMs / kernel logs.

Immediate mitigation options to propose (fastest first):
- Short-term: route Acme traffic to fallback model variant redwood-rt-1.3-legacy (config already exists) for reduced latency while we investigate. (Risk: slight quality delta)
- Scale-up: manually increase replicas in dedicated pool by +30% and temporarily disable aggressive downscale (SRE).
- Cache flush + warmup: force a controlled KV cache clear then run warmup traffic to repopulate. (Risk: transient higher latency during warmup)
- Circuit-breaker: enable per-route circuit breaker to fail fast and return graceful 429 to Acme if overload persists (ask product about acceptable UX).

Customer comms (draft message we can send during meeting):
"Hi Jenna (Acme SRE),
We see an elevated error rate and latency on your payment-authorization route. We're opening a dedicated war-room now and will keep you updated every 15 minutes. First actions: routing you to a low-latency fallback model and scaling up capacity to reduce errors. ETA for immediate mitigations: ~10-20 minutes. Will update with verification steps. — Ava / Redwood"
(we'll iterate live)

Roles & owners for war-room (assign now):
- Incident lead / customer comms: Ava Chen (owner) -> coordinates updates and sends messages to Acme.
- Runtime / serving lead: Diego Martinez -> run logs, validate error traces, propose rollback to legacy variant.
- SRE / infra: Priya Singh -> scale dedicated pool, check node health, inspect dmesg/kube events.
- Model lead: Tom Baker -> validate model artifact, compare recent build checksums, verify quantization path.
- CS escalation partner: Elena Rodriguez -> support customer questions, track CS tickets and impacts.
- QA / validation: (if needed) -> run smoke tests on fallback route, verify successful end-to-end auth flows.

Action items (captured during initial meeting - to convert to Jira after war-room):
- [Ava] Send first comms to customer and Slack #acme-incident. (due 2026-03-04 09:35 PT)
- [Diego] Collect last 3 hours of runtime logs & attach key error spans to Confluence ACME-Root-Cause. (due 2026-03-04 09:45 PT)
- [Priya] Temporarily scale dedicated-acme-1 pool +30% and pause downscaler. Confirm impact on latency. (due 2026-03-04 09:40 PT)
- [Tom] Verify model artifact for redwood-rt-1.3 (checksum + recent CI results) and test redwood-rt-1.3-legacy fallback on staging. (due 2026-03-04 10:00 PT)
- [Elena] Open a customer-facing status page entry and coordinate CS ticket updates. (due 2026-03-04 09:50 PT)
- [Ava/Priya] If scale-up not sufficient within 15m, flip traffic to fallback variant (announce to customer first). (decision point by 09:55 PT)
- [All] Document every step, time, and observed metric in the incident log. (continuous)

Notes-to-self / rough checklist to run during meeting:
- Have the fallback flag ready in routing config (route: acme-auth-v1 -> redwood-rt-1.3-legacy). Know the toggle path in Console and can roll back.
- Confirm rollback impact: token cost differences, expected QA delta.
- Keep SRE on quick pager for node-level reboots if kernel OOMs found.
- Confirm that Dedicated pool metrics in Grafana are showing per-instance queue lengths (to detect hot-shard).
- If we suspect cache corruption, do NOT mass-delete cache keys without warmup plan.

Follow-ups after war-room (post-mortem draft items):
- Timeline of events + key metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, failed transactions count).
- Root cause analysis: primary + contributing factors.
- Action plan: config changes, runtime hardening, autoscaler tuning, model validation checks, new monitoring alerts.
- Customer remediation: SLA credits? manual reconciliations? Proposal to Acme CS.
- Prevention: automated canary for model variant with warmup verification; KV cache integrity checks; autoscaler guard-rails.

Unresolved questions (to ask during meeting):
- Were there any infra maintenance windows or kernel updates on 2026-03-03 evening? (Priya)
- Any recent changes to cache eviction policy or memory thresholds on dedicated-acme-1? (Diego/Tom)
- Does Acme have bursty traffic pattern scheduled historically at this time? (Elena to verify)

Misc notes / links to paste in war-room chat:
- Confluence incident page: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/CS/ACME-Root-Cause
- Jira: CS-4821 (incident tracking)
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01ABCDEF/p1670000000000000
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/ACME-DEDI-POOL

Quick personal checklist before joining call:
- Grab latest logs and paste top 10 error spans into Confluence.
- Draft first customer comms (short + honest + ETA + next update cadence).
- Confirm backup routing toggle is tested in staging and I know the exact Console clicks.

-- end of prep notes --

(Will convert actions to Jira tasks after war-room and update this doc with final timeline + post-mortem link.)
